inputs.label: Ammonium band
inputs.coverage: 3.1 µm NH4 (ammonium) band depth, 1 - Rc/Rb (Clark and Roush), with the continuum of Frigeri et al. (2019): from the maximum in 2.91-3.01 µm to the maximum in 3.19-3.24 µm. Reduced here from Dawn VIR calibrated cubes: per-line SPICE cameras, I/F with the archive solar spectrum, three-channel boxcar, column stripes and spikes removed, cubes brought to 30° phase, pixel footprints mapped, seams blended as ISIS3 noseam does, incidence and emission below 70° (Ciarniello et al. 2017), overlaps averaged. Survey and HAMO cubes set every cell they saw; LAMO, then Approach cubes no coarser than the coarsest Survey cube, fill only cells those missed; cubes that disagree with all neighbours are levelled by their measured offset and used last. 16 pixels per degree, 60°S to 60°N, 98.7% covered; unmeasured cells hold -1.0E+32.

references.evidence: 1,657 calibrated IR cubes (672 Survey and HAMO, 875 LAMO, 110 Approach) listed in science/vir-reduction/recipe.json and named in science/vir-reduction/receipt.json.

The fitted band-depth change per degree of phase angle, each cube's phase from the archive's geometry index, and the 17 cubes rejected as outliers (modified z-score over 3.5).
Hapke model of Ceres in the Dawn FC F3 filter at 749 nm, the colour filter nearest the clear-filter mosaic, used to light the globe.

references.evidence: Li et al. (2019) eq. 1 to 3 define the Hapke model: Hapke (1984) roughness, the Hapke (2002) H function and a two-term Henyey-Greenstein phase function whose first lobe, weighted (1 + c)/2, scatters backward. Table 1, F3 row, gives w 0.139, b 0.364, c 0.048 and roughness 19.2 degrees, with B0 1.6 and h 0.06 held fixed at the values of Helfenstein and Veverka (1989). Section 2.2 discards data with incidence or emission above 80 degrees; section 4 says the fitted phase angles run from about 7 to about 95 degrees. Values were read in the accepted manuscript, arXiv:1812.08361.
references.locator: Eq. 1 to 3; Table 1, F3 row; sections 2.2 and 4
